examples.question: Reference: RFI 27 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Striping Along Curb at Accessible Parking (Main Entry) Confirmation Attached Pictures Enlarged Site Plans Mark Up During site demolition, it was noticed that if the plan directions were followed and the stripe along the face of curb got installed, the crosswalk would be at an angle, and it would require demo of existing special aggregate exposed concrete. See attached pictures for clarity. Question: Please confirm it is acceptable to instead stripe in alignment with the existing concrete. (Approximately 23 inches left of existing black tiles).
examples.resolution: Ava Ghiassi: Please see attached PDF.
root_causes: The stripe along the face of the curb, if installed according to the plan, would result in the crosswalk being at an angle, necessitating the demolition of existing special aggregate exposed concrete.
Impact: Requires additional work to demo existing concrete to align the crosswalk properly, leading to increased costs.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct a thorough site assessment to identify existing conditions that may conflict with design plans before finalizing the striping layout.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 46 Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Added Bike Racks Clarification RFI 26.1 Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Chipping of Concrete Footings Confirmation R_1 During OAC call on 2/25, Abbott confirmed that the no parking area highlighted in RFI 46 is to get added Bike Racks. Please confirm the Spec, Dimensioned location, Quantities, and mounting details for proposed Bike racks.
examples.resolution: Ava Ghiassi: Please see attached PDF.
root_causes: Addition of bike racks in a no parking area as confirmed during OAC call
Impact: Requires specification, dimensioned location, quantities, and mounting details for bike racks
examples.prevention_action: Incorporate bike rack requirements in initial design and confirm with stakeholders during design phase

examples.question: Reference: RFI 47 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Restrooms Existing Conditions Confirmations Attached Pictures with Markups Sheet A4.4.0 Drawing sheet A4.4.0 provides design intent for the 2nd floor restrooms. DPR was contracted to only provide new finishes in these restrooms. However, additional work needs to be completed due to the existing conditions of the framing. Question 1: Existing framing only goes to 8' height. RCP calls for 9' ceilings. Per OAC on 02/27/25, DPR to proceed with 9' ceilings. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 2: Plumbing will need to be removed to install the new 3 5/8" studs (@ 10' tall for the 9' ceilings) and re- installed after framing is complete. Per OAC on 02/27/25, DPR to with removal and re-install of plumbing due to new framing installation. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 3: Per OAC on 02/27/25, DPR to proceed with shifting of plumbing carriers plan north to accommodate the ADA stall layout. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 4: Concrete wall calls for paint. Imperfections will be very noticeable if the wall is only primed and painted. Per OAC on 02/27/25, DPR to proceed with adding hat channels and drywall at this location to create a finished surface. Furred wall will have a total thickness of 1-1/2" off concrete wall. Please confirm no exceptions.
examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu: Work is approved with no exceptions, see attached for additional comments.
root_causes: Existing framing only goes to 8' height while RCP calls for 9' ceilings.
Impact: Requires removal and re-installation of plumbing to accommodate new 10' tall studs for the 9' ceilings.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct thorough existing conditions survey prior to finalizing design and scope.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 69 - Phase 1B Restrooms Existing Conditions Modifications Confirmation Detail 1/A4.4.0 Attached Pictures with Markups Similar to the restrooms in Phase 1A, the only scope of work was to add new finishes to the walls, floors, ceilings, and installation of new plumbing fixtures, partitions, and counters. However, after doing the initial demolition, DPR noticed that the same issues were being observed in the Phase 1B restrooms. Please see the attached pictures and confirm if the proposed modifications are acceptable. Question 1: Concrete wall calls for paint (once tile is removed). Imperfections will be very noticeable if the wall is only primed and painted. DPR proceeded with adding hat channels and drywall at this location to create a finished surface. Furred wall will have a total thickness of 1-1/2" off concrete wall. Please confirm no exceptions taken to doing the same for restrooms in Phase 1B. Question 2: Similar to the restrooms in Phase 1A, please confirm DPR is to proceed with providing new plumbing carriers at the wet walls. These carriers will need to be relocated once installed to accommodate the ADA stall layout. Question 3: Existing framing only goes to 8' height. RCP calls for 9' ceilings. Please confirm no exceptions for DPR to proceed with re-framing walls to accommodate the 9' ceilings. Question 4: Existing transfer duct in the restrooms, neither do the demo plans nor do the mechanical plans mention a transfer duct within this space. Please confirm if transfer air ducts are to stay in place. Please also confirm if new ceiling grille (similar to CEF-1) is required for the transfer air ducts. Question 5: Similar to Phase 1A restrooms, plumbing will need to be removed to install the new 3 5/8" studs (@ 10' tall for the 9' ceilings) and re-installed after framing is complete. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 7: Per CBF, electrical receptacles in men's and women's restrooms (Phase 1B) will need be upgraded as the current circuits are not code compliant. The existing feeds do not have ground, and the existing conductors are undersized. New home runs will need to be pulled back to the panel. Panel B circuits 3 and 5 are being utilized. Please confirm no exceptions. Question 8: Existing electrical conduit is currently sitting on top of the 8' ceiling framing. Please confirm it is acceptable to remove the conduit and replace it with flex where needed and provide proper supports per code.
examples.resolution: Ava Ghiassi (FORGE - 10049724): Please see attached PDF.
root_causes: Existing framing only goes to 8' height while RCP calls for 9' ceilings.
Impact: Requires re-framing of walls to accommodate the 9' ceilings, leading to additional labor and material costs.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct a thorough review of existing conditions and verify framing heights during pre-construction surveys.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 76 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Stair 2 Slab Edge Infill Confirmation A7.0.0 Attached pictures Actual length of existing landing is 5'-11 3/4". This will cause the stair to be shorter at the bottom if left as is, and the footings would need to be relocated to accommodate this new dimension. DPR proposes to infill the delta of 13-1/4" with wood. The wood infill can be supported by the new wood wall that is to be installed to support the stairs. Please confirm if this is acceptable. If so, please provide connection details for wood infill to wood stud wall below.
examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu (FORGE - 10049724): See attached for detailed comments.
root_causes: Actual length of existing landing is 5'-11 3/4" which is shorter than the designed stair dimensions.
Impact: Requires relocation of footings to accommodate the new stair dimension, leading to additional work and costs.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct a thorough survey of existing conditions prior to finalizing design dimensions.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 74.1 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Stair 2 Shoring Detail Clarification RFI 74 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Stair 2 WF Beam to (E) OWJ Connection at Top and Bottom of Opening Clarification Marked up Picture Detail 2/S2.01 Per RFI 74 response, OWJ trusses at top and bottom of slab opening (red) need to reattach to the new W14x34 beam. To do this, DPR needs to remove the existing OWJ truss (blue), however once the truss is removed, it will leave the perpendicular truss (red) and slab hanging. Therefore, shoring of the slab will be required prior to completely removing the existing truss. DPR is proposing a layout of (2) shoring posts at each end as shown in the planview detail 2/S2.01. DPR is proposing to use Pro-Shore shoring, see product data attached. SEOR to confirm shoring detail is acceptable.
examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu (FORGE - 10049724): SEE ATTACHED FOR TIPPING'S DETAILED RESPONSE.
root_causes: Existing OWJ truss needs to be removed to reattach to the new W14x34 beam, leaving the perpendicular truss and slab unsupported.
Impact: Requires shoring of the slab to prevent it from hanging unsupported after the removal of the existing truss.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct a thorough review of existing structural conditions and support requirements during design phase.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 108 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Stair 1 Added L-Bracket Clarifications ASK-22 Stair 1 Guardrail and Handrail Submittal L-Bracket anchored to slab was added in RFI 103 response and Guardrail/Handrail Submittal, but no details showing the extent of install was provided. 1. Please provide structural details for anchoring into slab. 2. Please also provide details on how the L-Bracket interacts with the wall panel under the stair when the bracket returns to the wall.
examples.resolution: Elaine Yiu (FORGE - 10049724): M. TYE SEE ATTACHED FOR STRUCTURAL RESPONSE AND ASK-25 FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION.
root_causes: No details showing the extent of install for the L-Bracket anchoring into the slab and its interaction with the wall panel under the stair were provided.
Impact: Lack of structural details led to uncertainty in installation, requiring additional work to clarify anchoring methods and interactions.
examples.prevention_action: Ensure comprehensive structural details are included in submittals and RFIs to clarify installation requirements.

examples.question: Reference: RFI 16 - Abbott Alameda 1420 HBP - Seismic Anchorage Detail for HVAC Equipment Confirmation Bid Addendum #1 Mechanical Drawings As per the Mechanical Drawings M0.2 Details 2 & 3, seismic bracing is not shown on the air terminal and exhaust fan hanging details. From the mechanical schedule these units' weights' range from: VAVs - 86 - 166 lbs EFs - 47 - 65 lbs These units will require seismic per code. Please provide seismic bracing details for this equipment. If MHC/Forge would like to delegate this design to ACCO/DPR please refer to Alternate #10 provided in DPR's proposal (rejected at bid time).
examples.resolution: James Watters: See attached response.
root_causes: Seismic bracing details for HVAC equipment not shown on mechanical drawings M0.2 Details 2 & 3
Impact: Units require seismic bracing per code, which was not accounted for in the original design
examples.prevention_action: Ensure all seismic requirements are included in mechanical drawings during design phase

examples.question: Architectural drawing P3-A02-01A calls for RAF in Stair 2 251 and Fiber 272 with a callout stating "V.I.F. PULL BOXES RAISED 3'" in Fiber 272. Per 5/28 coordination meeting with Corgan/DPR, it was determined that bottom of the fiber pull box is 4' above slab and RAF should cover the entirety of the room. Additionally, there is an existing IDU and j-box above the door 272. The height from top of door 272 frame to bottom of j-box is 29". If the door and frame are to be raised 3', the existing j-box, IDU, Thermostat, and associated refrigerant piping will need to be raised accordingly. Suggested answer Corgan, please confirm the following 1. Fiber 272 and Stair 2 251 are to have RAF per the latest P3-A02-01A sheet, revision 04.30.2025 CITY COMMENT RESPONSE #1. 2. The existing fiber pull box does not need to be raised. 3. The fire rated plywood needs to be raised to 8' above RAF and re-painted 4. If the existing light fixtures and receptacles in Fiber 272 and Stair 251 need to be raised 3' accordingly. kW, please confirm if refrigerant piping that is to be raised between existing mechanical equipment will need to be pressure tested. CoreSite DCO, please confirm if 0272-IDU-05-01 (E) and 0251-BSU-05-01 (E) can be temporarily deactivated to be raised along with connecting refrigerant piping. If so, MOP will be processed accordingly.
examples.resolution: Abdul Mohi Mohammed (KW Engineering - 10059720): KW Response ELECTRICAL: Existing receptacle to be mounted at 1’-6” AFF. Relocate as required. Existing light fixture to be mounted at 12’-0” AFF. Light switch to be mounted at 48” AFF. Relocate as required. Created
root_causes: Existing j-box and IDU above door 272 are at a height of 29 inches from the top of the door frame, conflicting with the requirement to raise the door and frame by 3 feet.
Impact: Requires raising existing j-box, IDU, thermostat, and associated refrigerant piping to accommodate the new door height, leading to additional work and costs.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct thorough coordination meetings and site surveys to identify existing conditions before finalizing design changes.

Please confirm it is acceptable to remove the conduit and replace it with flex where needed and provide proper supports per code.

examples.question: Architectural drawing P3-A02-01A calls for RAF in Stair 2 251 and Fiber 272 with a callout stating "V.I.F. PULL BOXES RAISED 3'" in Fiber 272. Per 5/28 coordination meeting with Corgan/DPR, it was determined that bottom of the fiber pull box is 4' above slab and RAF should cover the entirety of the room. Additionally, there is an existing IDU and j-box above the door 272. The height from top of door 272 frame to bottom of j-box is 29". If the door and frame are to be raised 3', the existing j-box, IDU, Thermostat, and associated refrigerant piping will need to be raised accordingly. Suggested answer Corgan, please confirm the following 1. Fiber 272 and Stair 2 251 are to have RAF per the latest P3-A02-01A sheet, revision 04.30.2025 CITY COMMENT RESPONSE #1. 2. The existing fiber pull box does not need to be raised. 3. The fire rated plywood needs to be raised to 8' above RAF and re-painted 4. If the existing light fixtures and receptacles in Fiber 272 and Stair 251 need to be raised 3' accordingly. kW, please confirm if refrigerant piping that is to be raised between existing mechanical equipment will need to be pressure tested. CoreSite DCO, please confirm if 0272-IDU-05-01 (E) and 0251-BSU-05-01 (E) can be temporarily deactivated to be raised along with connecting refrigerant piping. If so, MOP will be processed accordingly.
examples.resolution: Abdul Mohi Mohammed (KW Engineering - 10059720): KW Response ELECTRICAL: Existing receptacle to be mounted at 1’-6” AFF. Relocate as required. Existing light fixture to be mounted at 12’-0” AFF. Light switch to be mounted at 48” AFF. Relocate as required. Created
root_causes: Existing j-box and IDU above door 272 are at a height of 29 inches from the top of the door frame, conflicting with the requirement to raise the door and frame by 3 feet.
Impact: Requires raising existing j-box, IDU, thermostat, and associated refrigerant piping to accommodate the new door height, leading to additional work and costs.
examples.prevention_action: Conduct thorough coordination meetings and site surveys to identify existing conditions before finalizing design changes.

examples.question: Reference: Offsite Drawing C10.0 detail 4 Offsite Drawing 4/C10.0(SSF Standard R-2A) Curb and Gutters are to be placed per City Standard Detail R-1. City Specification R-1 states that expansion joints shall be construction at a maximum of 50' intervals in concrete curbs, gutters, sidewalks, and at cold joints. On 9/8/23 we had a rebar inspection with City of SSF inspectors, Tony Corsetti and Amer Moussali. Based on our discussion, the inspector has directed DPR to install expansion Joints in Curb/Gutter and Sidewalk at a maximum of 20' interval per an upcoming revision to city Specs R-1, see attached. As such, there will be added cost for labor and materials. Please confirm DPR is to follow the instructions of the City of SSF inspector and install expansion joints in curb, gutter, and sidewalk at a maximum interval of 20'.
examples.resolution: Julia Morini (DES Architects & Engineers, Inc. - 10012655): Please see attached.
root_causes: City inspector directed installation of expansion joints at a maximum of 20' intervals instead of the previously specified 50' intervals in concrete curbs, gutters, and sidewalks.
Impact: Increased labor and material costs due to the need for additional expansion joints installation.
examples.prevention_action: Ensure updated city specifications are reviewed and incorporated into project plans before construction begins.

examples.question: Referenced Documents: RFI 0974, S2.1, Spec Section 071300.2.2.F Question: Per RFI 0974, Waterstop is required on the perimeter of all footings of the building. According to specification section 071300.2.2.F Below-Grade Sheet Waterproofing, Waterstop is also called out to be installed at the Control Joint between slab pours (along Gridline 9) to avoid additional water intrusion onto the slab. However, the VMS system is being installed on the overall footprint of the building in order to eliminate this possibility. Please confirm if Waterstop is still required at the control joint between slab pours on gridline 9 in addition to the VMS.
examples.resolution: Julia Morini (DES Architects & Engineers, Inc. - 10012655): Please see attached.
root_causes: Waterstop is required at the control joint between slab pours along Gridline 9, but the VMS system is being installed on the overall footprint of the building.
Impact: Uncertainty about the necessity of Waterstop at the control joint could lead to potential water intrusion onto the slab, despite the installation of the VMS system.
examples.prevention_action: Clarify waterproofing requirements during design phase to ensure compatibility between different systems.
